ratings_why.fun: The lead queue is a real puzzle and the late in-fight spikes are exciting, but only one End of Turn text speaks, so permanent growth is thin and Tiers 1-3 feel quiet.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because 'only your Front's text works' makes slot order the whole tribe: no Battlegrounds tribe switches its own text off, and death becomes a handoff queue.

verdict_why: Two cards still don't read cleanly (Herald chains, Lemen's 'current Health'), and the Matriarch build can't reach the Kit count its tier check prices.

points.text: Herald of the Herd next to another Herald is unclear: does the first Herald also get the text the second one copies, and how many times? Say whether copied text includes copied text.
Old Mother Lemen's Kits copy her 'current' Health, but it isn't said whether damage she takes in a fight lowers every Kit. Say it copies her stats without damage, or that it does lower them.

Kits are Lemmings, so any Kit in the front row becomes the Front and silences Old Mother Lemen; she gets at most two Kits in B2 and B3, far below the 5 the tier check prices. 'While this is your Front, Kits are never your Front' would let Ole the Learned feed her.

Permanent growth has one channel: one End of Turn speaker a turn, so late boards lean almost entirely on in-fight Banner. Making Herding Elder or Banner-Bearer Loud would give the mid game a second growth line without breaking the rule.

Gerd the Shouter makes the enemy chew through your Lemmings while non-Lemming front-liners stay untouched, which is the tribe's best defence; worth showing that in the build text, since it's what makes the cycle plan work.

standouts.why: Trailbreaker turns a death into a relay: buff the next leader, swap, and the queue moves on. It makes ordering a real choice.
The Front Lemming is the tribe's Brann, and the one-swap rule now makes it clean; chasing it shapes the whole build.
Cantor of the Edge makes every leader's death pay, the plainest picture of 'sacrifice so the rest go further'.

weakest.why: Kit-Minder fights Banner-Bearer and Herding Elder for the one End of Turn slot, and +1/+1 to Kits is the weakest use of it.
Thaw Nester gives one 1/1 a turn only while it leads, so it costs your fight's opener for very little.
Ole the Learned fills front gaps with Kits that become your Front, which works against Old Mother Lemen and most openers.

flags.note: Cantor raising the Banner, then golden Brother Onward under The Front Lemming, gives everyone four times the Banner in one fight. In-fight only, so it resets, but worth the owner's eye.
Herald copying a Herald: whether copied text chains is not said.
'Current Health' doesn't say whether her damage passes to the Kits mid-fight.
Enemies can only hit your Front, so non-Lemmings are safe until every Lemming falls; with Snow Hall Digger refilling Kits, the queue can stall enemy boards for a long time.
